issue: When deciding whether to authorize a second or successive federal habeas petition under 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(3), may the court of appeals consider whether the petition is time-barred under § 2244(d)?

sides.position: The court of appeals' gatekeeping review is limited to the § 2244(b) requirements (new claim, newly discovered facts or new retroactive rule). Timeliness under § 2244(d) is left to the district court.

The court of appeals may, in its discretion, consider § 2244(d) timeliness at the gatekeeping stage, because § 2244(b)(3)(C) says the court 'may' authorize a petition only if the § 2244(b) showing is made.
cases: Johnson v. Robert, 431 F.3d 992, 992–93 (7th Cir. 2005) (per curiam)
In re Hill, 437 F.3d 1080, 1083 (11th Cir. 2006) (per curiam)

this_court: May consider § 2244(d) timeliness at the gatekeeping stage in its discretion, siding with the five circuits that take that approach.
quote: Our sister circuits are split on the scope of our gatekeeping review.
